newsitem.title: JAPAN: EU says wants timetable on Japan insurance opening.
newsitem.headline: EU says wants timetable on Japan insurance opening.

text.p: Japan should provide a timetable for opening up its primary insurance sectors, the European Union's chief trade negotiator Sir Leon Brittan said on Monday.
"There should be a timetable for liberalisation of both the life and non-life markets," Brittan said after the fifth annual EU-Japan summit.

"We think it is both unbalanced and illogical simply to open up the small third sector to Japanese companies without proceeding with liberalisation of the very much larger life and non-life sectors, which are totally dominated by Japanese companies at the moment," he told a news conference.
Brittan, however, declined to comment directly on a U.S.-Japan dispute over Japan's implementation of the 1994 U.S.-Japan pact on insurance deregulation.

Washington has charged that Tokyo was poised to renege on the pact by opening up the niche market for cancer, nursing care and personal accident insurance, dominated by foreign firms, before liberalising primary sectors dominated by domestic firms. Japan's Finance Ministry was to announce later on Monday conditions for domestic life and non-life insurers' subsidiaries entering each others' sectors from October 1. It was expected to delay their entry into the third sector.
